metadata.name: afterbell_vault
metadata.description: Protection on a tokenized stock's next opening print, sold against signed quotes and settled by the first Pyth print after the bell

accounts.name: position
docs: Derived from the quote's nonce: a second purchase with the same quote fails here.

accounts.name: position_mint
docs: The position's NFT: no decimals, its metadata on the mint itself. The
vault mints one and then gives up the mint authority.

accounts.name: holder_token
docs: The allowance is revoked only if it's still this order's.

accounts.name: rate
docs: The rate of the round that filled the deposit, unless it's already filled.

accounts.name: rate
docs: The rate of the round that filled the redemption, unless it's already filled.

accounts.name: collateral_mint
docs: Classic SPL Token only: Token-2022 transfer fees and hooks would break the accounting.

accounts.name: share_mint
docs: The pool's shares, in the collateral's decimals, with their name on the mint itself.

accounts.name: keeper_token
docs: Where the keeper's tips go.

accounts.name: keeper
docs: Anyone: pays the new accounts' rent, as a buyer would.

accounts.name: price_update
docs: The stock's latest price, which the strikes are checked against.

accounts.name: rate
docs: The rate of the round that filled an earlier deposit request, if one is waiting.

accounts.name: rate
docs: The rate of the round that filled an earlier redemption request, if one is waiting.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Pays the rent of the round's rate record.

accounts.name: price_update
docs: `Account` checks this is owned by the Pyth receiver program, so its
contents were posted (and signature-checked) by Pyth, not by the caller.

types.name: FeedConfig
docs: Whether the vault sells protection on a Pyth feed, and the stock's ticker
(the positions' NFTs show it). Disallowing a feed stops new sales; positions
already sold still settle and pay.

types.name: Forfeited
docs: A position whose NFT was burned: nobody holds it, so its payout stays in the pool.

fields.name: amount
docs: What it would have paid.

types.name: Order
docs: A holder's standing order: protection on one stock renewed each night by any
keeper, within the holder's limits, paid from an allowance the holder gave
this account over their collateral. It is the quote's buyer; the NFT goes to
the holder.

fields.name: start_bps
docs: Where protection starts and stops, in bps below the price.

fields.name: until
docs: Renews for openings before this time.

fields.name: last_open_ts
docs: The last opening renewed for, kept across a cancel so it can't renew twice.

fields.name: allowance
docs: What renewals may spend in all: the order's allowance over the holder's collateral.

types.name: Paid
docs: A position paid out to whoever held its NFT (or refunded, if its series voided).

types.name: Params
docs: Settlement timings and risk limits. Changes wait for the next roll, so a
round runs to the end on the rules it started with.

fields.name: max_utilization_bps
docs: The most a round may lock, as a share of the pool at its roll.

fields.name: max_feed_bps
docs: The most one stock may lock in a round, as a share of the pool at its roll.

fields.name: keeper_tip_bps
docs: The keeper's cut of each premium, paid to whoever pays the position out.

types.name: Position
docs: One sale. Its address comes from the quote's nonce, so a quote buys once.
It's paid to whoever holds its NFT, and stays on-chain afterwards with what
it paid.

fields.name: mint
docs: Its NFT: a Token-2022 mint with a supply of one.

fields.name: number
docs: Numbered in order of sale, from 1.

fields.name: paid
docs: What it paid, and to whom: the payout, or the premium if its series voided.

fields.name: feed_id
docs: `FeedId` but avoid the type alias because of compatibility issues with Anchor's `idl-build` feature.

fields.name: publish_time
docs: The timestamp of this price update in seconds

fields.name: prev_publish_time
docs: The timestamp of the previous price update. This field is intended to allow users to
identify the single unique price update for any moment in time:
for any time t, the unique update is the one such that prev_publish_time < t <= publish_time.
Note that there may not be such an update while we are migrating to the new message-sending logic,
as some price updates on pythnet may not be sent to other chains (because the message-sending
logic may not have triggered). We can solve this problem by making the message-sending mandatory
(which we can do once publishers have migrated over).
Additionally, this field may be equal to publish_time if the message is sent on a slot where
where the aggregation was unsuccesful. This problem will go away once all publishers have
migrated over to a recent version of pyth-agent.

types.name: PriceUpdateV2
docs: A price update account. This account is used by the Pyth Receiver program to store a verified price update from a Pyth price feed.
It contains:
- `write_authority`: The write authority for this account. This authority can close this account to reclaim rent or update the account to contain a different price update.
- `verification_level`: The [`VerificationLevel`] of this price update. This represents how many Wormhole guardian signatures have been verified for this price update.
- `price_message`: The actual price update.
- `posted_slot`: The slot at which this price update was posted.

fields.name: open_ts
docs: Unix seconds of the 09:30 ET open the protection settles on.

fields.name: shares
docs: Shares with 6 decimals.

fields.name: upper
docs: Prices with 8 decimals.

fields.name: premium
docs: Collateral units.

fields.name: expiry
docs: Unix seconds after which the quote can't be used.

types.name: Request
docs: An underwriter's queued deposit and redemption, and what earlier rolls
filled for them to claim.

types.name: RoundRate
docs: The pool at the roll that ended a round: the price every request queued in
that round was filled at.

fields.name: assets
docs: The pool's assets and share supply at the roll. Shares convert at
(assets + 1) / (supply + 1): an empty pool starts at one share per unit.

types.name: Series
docs: Every position on one feed for one open settles together, on one price.

fields.name: price
docs: Settlement price with 8 decimals.

fields.name: lowest_lower
docs: The strikes sold, bounding the price it can settle at.

fields.name: locked
docs: Maximum payouts of its positions not yet paid out.

types.name: Vault
docs: An underwriters' pool selling protection in one collateral mint. Its token
account holds the pool, premiums, queued deposits and redemptions owed.
Deposits and redemptions are requests filled at `roll`, which ends a round
once everything it sold is paid out: nothing is at risk then, so the pool's
value is exact and nobody joins or leaves at a stale price.

fields.name: quoter
docs: The ed25519 key whose signature prices every sale.

fields.name: share_mint
docs: The pool's shares (Token-2022, minted by the vault) and the vault's own
account of them: queued redemptions wait there, filled deposits too.

fields.name: collateral_unit
docs: 10^decimals of the collateral mint.

fields.name: round
docs: The round in progress, its opening (0 until its first sale) and the
pool's assets at the roll that began it, which its risk limits use.

fields.name: round_unpaid
docs: Positions the round sold that aren't paid out yet. A position is paid
only once its series settles or voids, so zero means the round is over.

fields.name: locked
docs: The most the open positions could still pay.

fields.name: tips_owed
docs: Keepers' tips on positions not yet paid out.

fields.name: reserved_assets
docs: Filled redemptions not yet claimed.

fields.name: art_uri
docs: Where a position NFT's image is served: this plus the position's address.

types.name: VerificationLevel
docs: Pyth price updates are bridged to all blockchains via Wormhole.
Using the price updates on another chain requires verifying the signatures of the Wormhole guardians.
The usual process is to check the signatures for two thirds of the total number of guardians, but this can be cumbersome on Solana because of the transaction size limits,
so we also allow for partial verification.
This enum represents how much a price update has been verified:
- If `Full`, we have verified the signatures for two thirds of the current guardians.
- If `Partial`, only `num_signatures` guardian signatures have been checked.
# Warning
Using partially verified price updates is dangerous, as it lowers the threshold of guardians that need to collude to produce a malicious price update.
